references.text: Cain became very angry and killed his brother Abel. This is an early example of jealousy and hatred between siblings that leads to violence.
Esau hated Jacob because he received the blessing from their father, showing how parental favoritism can lead to deep enmity between siblings.
The brothers were jealous of Joseph, a direct continuation of the hatred described in verse 4, now intensified by Joseph's dreams.
Eliab, David's oldest brother, became angry and spoke to David with contempt, a parallel to older brothers' jealousy toward a favored younger brother.
David complains about being hated without just cause, a parallel to unjust hatred driven by envy, as Joseph's brothers hated him.
Pilate knew it was out of envy that they handed Jesus over. Envy as the driving force behind hostile actions is a parallel to the jealousy of Joseph's brothers.
The Acts of the Apostles refer directly to the patriarchs selling Joseph out of envy, a New Testament commentary confirming the motivation behind the brothers' hatred.
Fulfillment of the conflict: the brothers who could not speak kindly to him (37:4) now speak with him in reconciliation.
Theological parallel: The brothers' rejection of Joseph as an image of the people rejecting God's messenger.
Thematic parallel: Brothers who become angry or jealous of a favorite brother and refuse to acknowledge the father's love.
Thematic parallel: Envy and anger among brothers/disciples triggered by parental/leader favoritism.
